notes: The page continues an earlier sentence with choisi. In the opening transformation the manuscript reads g after remplace and an argument of ρ now kept uncertain as l₀/λ after the blind audit. The adjacent int(λ)u and expanded expression l₀^αgl₁^{-α} suggest possible authorial slips, but neither symbol is silently changed. The written hypothesis α ∈ Z-hat-star is likewise preserved.

The author states that relations (*) and (**) determine u from p and g. A three-row system computes the images of l₀, l₁ and l∞, annotating intermediate expressions with underbraces. The final result is crossed at the physical right edge and rewritten above it. The replacement lacks an opening parenthesis immediately after int. The precise parentheses and final exponent of the crossed version remain uncertain.

The marginal note says that the map automatically respects the structure à lacets with multiplier p. Its readable prose is retained, but the subject after que remains u/g/u_g because an upper u-like curve and a lower loop with descender coexist.

The lower calculations state the condition that the three generator images multiply to 1, expand the inner conjugations, simplify the product, and move g^{-1} to the left. One whole intermediate display is struck out. The following live display has unmatched written parentheses; the transcription preserves those strokes instead of balancing them.

The closing paragraph asserts that (*) and (**) hold by construction and that, for **, it is enough to verify the two members at l₀ and l₁. It uses the live abbreviation barred m and the written abbreviation mb. A 2-like mark after the first (*) remains unresolved against C’s suggested comma; subscript placement is retained as an explicit alternative, without being asserted.

All four C deletion/insertion states were individually checked: cancelled multiplie; doubtful cancelled les; cancelled system result and its insertion above; and the fully struck penultimate display. The latter is readable across the strike. No date or independent drawing is present. The handwritten manuscript number is 7. Il faut vérifier is the author’s stated verification obligation, not a report of verification by this reader.

The reading used only this page packet, the established notation supplied in it, and root’s messages about this same page. No OCR, external research, or other page was consulted for this assignment. No mathematical proof check or formal computation was completed; the report records the author’s assertions and literal symbols.

The main reader checked the representative-change calculation locally. From uρ=int(g)ρu and u′=int(λ)u one obtains u′ρ=int(λg)ρu, whereas ρu′=int(ρ(λ))ρu; hence g′=λgρ(λ)⁻¹ gives the required equality. With λ=l₀^α and ρ(l₀)=l₁ this expands to l₀^αgl₁^−α. Thus u rather than the written g is the object naturally replaced in the prose, and λ rather than the first preferred l₀ reading is the expected argument in the preceding display. The clear manuscript g remains unchanged; the later blind audit reopens the rho argument as l₀/λ, without using this calculation to settle it. The claim is this algebraic transformation only, without an independent uniqueness theorem for g.

A second local check expands inner conjugation in the boxed product: l₀^p(g l₁^p g⁻¹)(gρ(g)l∞^pρ(g)⁻¹g⁻¹)=l₀^p g l₁^pρ(g)l∞^pρ(g)⁻¹g⁻¹. Conjugating this product by g⁻¹ gives int(g⁻¹)(l₀^p)·l₁^p·int(ρ(g))(l∞^p). Therefore equality to 1 is equivalent in the two expressions. This supports the intended algebra while leaving the unmatched written parentheses intact; it does not prove that the map is an automorphism.

The blind audit also detects an unwritten de supplied by both witnesses after en termes, an omitted underline under la relation and the primed-loop equation, and a supplied comma between the final l0 and l1. The underline is the very same physical rule visible at the top of the following formula crop, as their overlapping source coordinates show. The formula is rendered with its three lower frame strokes and that preceding underline, without duplicating the one top rule. The first rho argument and the marginal subject are deliberately less certain after independent rereading. The existing algebra checks are unchanged and do not settle either glyph.
